title: What does your gymnastics coaching need next?
lede: Gymnastics coaching is an order of operations. Twelve questions about how you coach today, and you will know which rung you are standing on, why it matters, and one thing to do about it this week.

questions.q: An athlete's swing looks wrong. What usually happens next?
a: I can tell something is off but not what
I can name the fault after watching a few reps
I see it on the first rep and can name it
I see it, name it, and know which position it traces back to

questions.q: Two athletes fail the same movement for different reasons. How often do you catch that?
a: Rarely — they tend to get the same cue
Sometimes, usually thinking about it afterwards
Usually, while it is happening
Always — I go in expecting it and look for it

questions.q: You demonstrate a shape. How do your athletes' versions come back?
a: All over the place
Roughly similar, hard to say what is off
Close, and I can pick out the gaps
Consistent, because I check the same reference points every time

questions.q: How do you decide what an athlete works on next?
a: Whatever the class programme has that day
Whatever they are struggling with most
A progression I follow for that movement
A defined order I could explain and justify for any athlete

questions.q: An athlete wants muscle-ups and cannot hold a hollow. What do you do?
a: Let them work muscle-ups and keep the volume low
Give them some hollow work alongside
Hold the muscle-up work until the position is there
Take them back and rebuild the sequence in order

questions.q: If another coach took your athletes for a month, could they carry on?
a: No — most of it is in my head
Roughly, from what is on the whiteboard
Yes, the progression is written down
Yes, and they would know why each step comes where it does

questions.q: An athlete has strict strength but an inconsistent kip. Your approach?
a: More reps until it clicks
Show it again, slower
Break the timing into components and drill those
Work out which component is mistimed and coach that one

questions.q: How do you coach rhythm and timing?
a: I do not really — it comes with practice
Counting or tempo cues
Drills that isolate the timing
Constraints that make the right timing the only option available

questions.q: A dynamic skill falls apart under fatigue. What is your read?
a: They are tired
A conditioning problem
The timing degrades before the strength does
I know which part of the sequence goes first for that athlete

questions.q: How do you decide how much gymnastics volume an athlete gets?
a: Whatever is in the class workout
More for the ones who need it
A set weekly amount by level
Prescribed against what they are adapting to, and adjusted as it changes

questions.q: An athlete has clean positions and good timing but has stopped progressing. Why?
a: Not sure
Probably needs to train more
The dose is not matched to the adaptation
I would know which variable to change, and by how much

questions.q: How do you manage gymnastics intensity across a week?
a: It is not separated from the rest of their training
I keep an informal eye on it
I plan harder and easier days
I prescribe it deliberately against everything else they are doing
